name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Wednesday 9 May 1990 (English cryptic)

clue.text: Soft drinks — French newspaper's wrapped round one

indicators.note: something wrapped round another thing encloses it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Le Monde is the Paris daily, plus the S of the possessive
one as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone's fizzy drinks arrive wrapped in a copy of a Paris paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Monde is the leading Paris daily; the 's of the possessive supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonades are sweet carbonated beverages, the standard example of non-alcoholic soft drinks.

clue.text: Liberal full of swear-words? That's disgusting

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
oaths are swear-words, so full of them is oathful

explanation.surface: A foul-mouthed Liberal politician is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: Loathful is a rare old word with the same sense as loathsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathful describes something that provokes loathing, hence repulsive or revolting.

clue.text: Perhaps lead the writer to speak endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as me
to talk is to speak

explanation.surface: Perhaps the writer should take the lead and keep talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead is the heavy element, not leadership; 'Perhaps' signals that it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is one example of a metal, so the definition names a member of the class.

clue.text: Use of atomic weapons can awe far ruler terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dreadful sense that a distant ruler might frighten the world with atom bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear warfare is combat using atomic bombs and missiles, which the definition describes.

clue.text: Twosome study one or several parts of intestines

blocks.note: a duo is a pair
a den is a study, a private room for work
one as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pair studying one or more sections of the gut in anatomy class.
explanation.walkthrough: Duodena is the Latin plural of duodenum, which is why the definition says several.
explanation.definitionFit: Each duodenum is the first section of the small intestine, just after the stomach.

clue.text: Socialists' leader, confused and encumbered

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Socialists'
addled means muddled

explanation.surface: The head of the Socialists is muddled and weighed down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be saddled with something is to be burdened with it, so a synonym of encumbered.

clue.text: Large vessel for Sunday Joint

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A big pot in which to cook the Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday Joint' suggests a roast of meat; it is S plus a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship is a seagoing craft, bigger than a boat, so a large vessel.

clue.text: Mischievous imp has to go inside walk in awkwardly

indicators.note: inside places the short word within the longer one

blocks.note: hobblin', the clipped spoken form of hobbling, walking awkwardly
taken as written

explanation.surface: An imp is ordered to go in, limping clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: GO goes into HOBBLIN, which reads 'walk in awkwardly' as hobblin' with its G dropped, as it is often said.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous sprite of English folklore, such as Puck.

clue.text: Equal status I acquired in a company

indicators.note: acquired by and taken into a group, so one letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: a party is a group of people, a company
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joined a firm and won an equal standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality of rank or value, from the Latin par meaning equal.

clue.text: Where to find lidos, or the rays shimmering!

definitions.text: Where to find lidos, or the rays shimmering!

indicators.note: shimmering light wavers and breaks up, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Seaside places with open-air pools and sunlight glinting on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while its middle words supply the letters; a lido is a public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday resorts are towns built for leisure visitors, where pools and sunshine are the attraction.

clue.text: Cramped accommodation of Athens?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small room squeezed under the roof
second meaning: relating to Attica, the region round Athens

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is the adjective Attic, the classical word for Athenian.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft room under a sloping roof is tight on space, and Attic is the adjective for ancient Athens and its dialect.

clue.text: Peculiar broker, one doing occasional bits of work

definitions.text: one doing occasional bits of work

blocks.note: odd means strange
a jobber was a dealer on the London Stock Exchange

explanation.surface: A strange stockbroker who only does the occasional job.
explanation.walkthrough: A stockjobber traded shares on the London exchange before 1986; jobber alone also means one who does odd jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-jobber is a handyman hired for small casual tasks now and then.

clue.text: Greek ambassador enthralling Terry?

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so one piece holds the other within it

blocks.note: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
Ellen Terry, the Victorian stage actress; the question mark flags a surname standing for a first name

explanation.surface: A Greek diplomat captivated by someone called Terry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek person, from Hellas, the Greeks' own name for their country.

clue.text: Felled the boor without help

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece stands around the other

blocks.note: a lout is an uncouth man
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: Someone knocked down the oaf single-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without help' reads as unaided, but without here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay someone out is to knock them flat with a blow, so laid out is a synonym of felled.

clue.text: Delivery, legal at cricket, deceitful at a dance

blocks.note: underhand means sly or dishonest
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A contrast between honest play at cricket and trickery on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets legal against deceitful, but deceitful is just a synonym; the definition is the whole first part.
explanation.definitionFit: An underhand ball is bowled with the arm below the shoulder, an old style still within cricket's laws.

clue.text: The Queen comes in to make wares for well-meaning reformers

indicators.note: something that comes in enters, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: do as make, goods as wares
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: The monarch visits to see goods being manufactured.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-gooders are earnest people trying to improve society, often naively; the term mixes praise and mockery.

clue.text: End seems uncertain for landed estates

indicators.note: uncertain suggests nothing is settled, so the order of these letters is not fixed

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The future of the great country houses looks shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held and worked by its owner, especially the grounds around a manor.

clue.text: What a film-star makes, arriving last? £1,000, with charm

definitions.text: What a film-star makes, arriving last?

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
to entrance is to enchant, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: A movie star turns up late, paid a fortune and full of charm.
explanation.walkthrough: The charm sense is the verb entrance, which is spelt like the noun for a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A star who arrives last sweeps in for maximum attention, a showy arrival known by this idiom.

clue.text: Walked over, circumventing soldier at rest

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round
circumventing means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: trod is the past tense of tread
a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Someone strolled past a soldier who was off duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walked over' looks like a phrasal verb, but over is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or asleep, as a volcano or seed is at rest.

clue.text: It's a cold wintry wind, and not the end of summer

indicators.note: the end is the last position, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: nor means and not
taken as written
the last letter of summer

explanation.surface: A cold winter wind blows, nothing like summer's close.
explanation.definitionFit: A norther is a strong cold gale from the north, especially in Texas and the Gulf.

clue.text: Forcibly remove revolting king, excessively uppity

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: up as in up in arms, in revolt
R for rex, Latin for king
too means to excess

explanation.surface: Rebels oust an arrogant king who has got above himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Uppity looks like an adjective for the king, but it signals that TOO reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull out by the roots, so to remove people or things by force.

clue.text: Present couple put before one

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
to offer something is to put it before someone

explanation.surface: A gift handed over by a pair who come first.
explanation.walkthrough: Present is the verb here, stressed on the second syllable, not the noun meaning a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to hold something out for acceptance, a formal synonym of the verb present.

clue.text: One pound given over in pay increase? Ludicrous

indicators.note: something turned over shows its other end first, so the pound's letters run backwards
in places the preceding pieces inside the pay increase

blocks.note: a rise is the British word for a raise in salary
Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A pay rise of only one pound would be laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the pound's abbreviation turns round; I then BL sit inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, from the Latin for laughing, so it is a synonym of ludicrous.

clue.text: Name inscribed in great English party

indicators.note: something inscribed in is written within, so the letter sits inside

blocks.note: big means great in size
E is the abbreviation for English
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A name is engraved for a grand English celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spree of heavy drinking or eating, so a wild party.

clue.text: Outwit along stretch of river

blocks.note: over in the sense of across or along a surface
a reach is a straight stretch of a river between bends

explanation.surface: Getting the better of someone on a walk along the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach someone is an old use meaning to get the better of them by cunning.

clue.text: No railway association needs backing to keep talking

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters before it are read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A railway union refuses its support to an endless debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To run on is to go on speaking at length without stopping, an idiom for chattering.

clue.text: Tooth sunk into succulent US kebab

indicators.note: something sunk into a phrase is buried inside it, running across the word boundaries

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of succulent, all of US and the start of kebab

explanation.surface: Someone bites into a juicy American kebab.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusk is the long protruding tooth of an elephant, walrus or boar.

clue.text: They beat most of the less cautious players, ultimately

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word that follows
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
rasher is the comparative of rash
the last letter of players

explanation.surface: Bold players get beaten by those who take more risks.
explanation.walkthrough: Rasher looks like bacon but is the comparative of rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashers are people who thrash, that is beat or flog, so they beat.
